name_reason: Verb-phrase descriptive name consistent with the input/timing family in this file (fd2_wait_n_bios_ticks, fd2_read_bios_midnight_tick, fd2_wait_for_input_v2). 'wait_one_bios_tick' precisely states the behavior: block until the BIOS midnight tick (0:046C) advances by exactly one step. No Ghidra address-residue suffix; no embedded domain ID to preserve. Parallel to its sibling fd2_wait_n_bios_ticks -- renaming would break the established family naming.
purpose: Busy-spin frame pacer that blocks until the BIOS midnight tick (0:046C, 18.2 Hz) advances at least one step (~55 ms), then caches the new tick for the next call.
logic_summary: Spins while the live BIOS tick equals the cached last-seen value, then stores the new tick. The tick is read SIGN-EXTENDED to 32 bits at both sites (asm: MOVSX EAX,word ptr [0x46C]) and compared/stored as a full dword (CMP EAX,dword ptr [0x53A0C] / MOV [0x53A0C],EAX), so a low word of 0xFFFF caches as 0xFFFFFFFF -- not a plain 16-bit dword read. The cached state data_fd2_engine_wait_one_bios_tick_last_seen (0x53A0C) persists across calls, so each call waits for the tick following the one observed last time. Leading PUSH 4 / CALL __CHK is the Watcom stack-probe prologue, not game logic (the in_stack_* args in the decompile are the probe's garbage stack reads, not real parameters).

returns.semantics: No return value; effect is the busy-wait of one BIOS tick plus the side-effect of updating data_fd2_engine_wait_one_bios_tick_last_seen.

reads_globals: BIOS_TICK_WORD (BDA 0:0x46C, low word of the 18.2 Hz midnight tick counter; read sign-extended)
writes_globals: data_fd2_engine_wait_one_bios_tick_last_seen (0x53A0C, stores the newly observed sign-extended tick)
